message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 340, "amount_cents": 9785}, {"order_id": 341, "amount_cents": 12369}, {"order_id": 345, "amount_cents": 12076}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: I need to verify that the refunds reported by Alpha Co match the refunds in my system before recording any payouts. I will call list_refunds to compare.

The refunds reported by Alpha Co match exactly what I have in my refunds list, so I can proceed to record payouts for each customer. I need to call net_balance for each customer to get the amount to pay.
The net_balance call failed because customer CUST_340 does not exist. I need to find which customers are associated with the refunded orders. I will list the orders to see the customer IDs.
I now see that the customers are acme, birch, and cobalt. I need to call net_balance for each of these customers to get the amount to pay.
I have the net balance for acme (30272 cents). Now I need to get the net balance for birch and cobalt.
I have net balances for acme (30272) and birch (16317). Now I need the net balance for cobalt.
I have net balances for all customers: acme 30272, birch 16317, cobalt 17328. I will now record the payouts for each customer.
The payout for acme (30272) was recorded successfully. I need to record payouts for birch (16317) and cobalt (17328).

result.error: bad arguments: World.record_payout() got an unexpected keyword argument 'amount_cent'. Did you mean 'amount_cents'?

reply.thought: I made a typo in the argument name. The correct field is 'amount_cents'. I will correct it and record the payout for birch.
The payout for birch (16317) was recorded successfully. I need to record the payout for cobalt (17328) to complete all customer payouts.
All payouts have been recorded successfully. The batch is complete. I will now finalize with a report of the payouts.
